precios.nota: Claude Code escribe caché con TTL de 1 h (2x input); el de 5 min cuesta 1.25x. Lectura de caché 0.1x input, salvo Fable 5.1, que la documenta a $0.25.

comentariosJueces.opus: D and G are a notch above the rest: D for its flawless itinerary and coherent identity, and G for its homepage and the most creative ideas, though with some visual excess. B is the most elegant and polished, but its alerts are less complete; C is the most logically correct after D, with a more generic aesthetic. A and E have good ideas (rain notice, per-venue grid) with less polish, F has confusing details and poor posters, and H works but feels like a template. The most common failure was not flagging that the Q&A is missed when you also don't make it in time (5 of 8 teams).
comentariosJueces.fable: All eight handle the itinerary logic with almost no errors; what separates the table is the visual identity, how they represent films without a poster, and how much they thought about the port audience with a phone in hand. G and D are clearly on top: both have a distinctive graphic idea, posters with a system, and an itinerary with summaries and actions that feel considered (By venue, tickets, remove one, rain contingency). B and A are very solid and well aligned but with less surprise; C sits a notch below because of the misleading case 2 label and repetitive posters. E meets everything and has the best per-venue grid, but with an understated identity; F is correct but generic, with the rain notice reversed; H closes out the list because it works but looks like a corporate template, pastes the brief onto the homepage, and doesn't solve films without a poster.
